title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 72 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 450–452 (Night 72, continuing directly from nights-71), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 72 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. In Baghdad the eunuch searches for the unseen singer and finds only the stoker awake; Ḍawʾ al-Makān, roused by the night breeze, defies the stoker’s warnings and recites two sets of verses of longing, and Nuzhat al-Zamān, hearing her own and her brother’s names in them, sends the servant out again with gold. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāniyatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the second and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-second night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْ مِنْ أَخِيهَا الشِّعْرَ دَعَتِ الْخَادِمَ الْكَبِيرَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ اذْهَبْ وَائْتِنِي بِمَنْ يُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna nuzhata al-zamāni lammā samiʿat min akhīhā al-shiʿra daʿati al-khādima al-kabīra wa-qālat lahu idhhab wa-ʾtinī bi-man yunshidu hādhihi al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Nuzhat al-Zamān, when she heard from her brother the poetry, called the servant the great, and said to him: Go, and bring-me with-whoever recites these poems.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard her brother’s verses, she called the chief servant and said to him: Go and bring me whoever is reciting these poems.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); read as two words. بمن after وائتني: the bi- marks the person fetched (“bring me with him”).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنِّي لَمْ أَسْمَعْهُ وَلَمْ أَعْرِفْهُ وَالنَّاسُ كُلُّهُمْ نَائِمُونَ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ كُلُّ مَنْ رَأَيْتَهُ مُسْتَيْقِظًا فَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنْشِدُ الْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā innī lam asmaʿhu wa-lam aʿrifhu wa-al-nāsu kulluhum nāʾimūna fa-qālat lahu kullu man raʾaytahu mustayqiẓan fa-huwa alladhī yunshidu al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: And he said to her: Indeed I, I have not heard him, and I have not known him, and the people, all-of-them, (are) sleepers. And she said to him: Every who you have seen awake — he (is) the one who recites the poems.
sentences.i: He said to her: I have not heard him and I do not know him, and the people are all asleep. She said to him: Anyone you find awake is the one who is reciting the poems.

sentences.t: فَفَتَّشَ فَلَمْ يَرَ مُسْتَيْقِظًا سِوَى الرَّجُلِ الْوَقَّادِ وَضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فَإِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي غَشْيَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fattasha fa-lam yara mustayqiẓan siwā al-rajuli al-waqqādi wa-ḍawʾu al-makāni fa-innahu kāna fī ghashyatihi
sentences.l: So he searched, and did not see one awake except the man the stoker; and Ḍawʾ al-Makān — for he was in his swoon.
sentences.i: So he searched, and found no one awake except the stoker; as for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, he was still in his swoon.
sentences.n: The print reads “except the stoker and Ḍawʾ al-Makān”, but Ḍawʾ al-Makān is then said to be unconscious; the sentence is read as a fresh clause, “and as for Ḍawʾ al-Makān …”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْوَقَّادُ الْخَادِمَ وَاقِعًا عَلَى رَأْسِهِ خَافَ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ هَلْ أَنْتَ الَّذِي كُنْتَ تُنْشِدُ الشِّعْرَ وَقَدْ سَمِعَتْكَ سَيِّدَتُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-waqqādu al-khādima wāqiʿan ʿalā raʾsihi khāfa minhu fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu hal anta alladhī kunta tunshidu al-shiʿra wa-qad samiʿatka sayyidatunā
sentences.l: And when the stoker saw the servant fallen upon his head, he feared from him; and the servant said to him: Is it you, the one who were reciting the poetry? — and our lady has heard you.
sentences.i: When the stoker saw the servant standing over him, he was afraid of him. The servant said to him: Was it you who was reciting the verses? Our lady has heard you.
sentences.n: واقعا على رأسه is an Egyptian idiom, “planted over his head”, i.e. standing right over him.

sentences.t: فَاعْتَقَدَ الْوَقَّادُأَنَّ السِّتَّ اغْتَاظَتْ مِنْ إِنْشَادِ الشِّعْرِ فَخَافَ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَاللَّهِ مَا هُوَ أَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʾtaqada al-waqqādu anna al-sitta ightāẓat min inshādi al-shiʿri fa-khāfa wa-qāla lahu wa-allāhi mā huwa anā
sentences.l: And the stoker believed that the lady was enraged at the reciting of the poetry; so he feared, and said to him: By God, it is not I.
sentences.i: The stoker supposed that the lady had been angered by the recitation, and he took fright and said: By God, it was not I.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the previous word (الوقادان); read “the stoker — that”. السِّتّ “the lady” is Egyptian colloquial usage.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ وَمَنْ هُوَ الَّذِي كَانَ يُنْشِدُ فَدُلَّنِي عَلَيْهِ فَأَنْتَ تَعْرِفُهُ لِأَنَّكَ يَقْظَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu wa-man huwa alladhī kāna yunshidu fa-dullanī ʿalayhi fa-anta taʿrifuhu li-annaka yaqẓānu
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: And who is the one who was reciting? So guide-me to him, for you know him, because you (are) awake.
sentences.i: The servant said to him: Then who was it who was reciting? Show me where he is — you must know him, since you are awake.

sentences.t: فَخَافَ الْوَقَّادُ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ رُبَّمَا أَنَّ الْخَادِمَ يَضُرُّهُ بِشَيْ فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَمْ أَعْرِفْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-khāfa al-waqqādu ʿalā ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-qāla fī nafsihi rubbamā anna al-khādima yaḍurruhu bi-shayʾin fa-qāla wa-allāhi lam aʿrifhu
sentences.l: And the stoker feared for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and said in his soul: Perhaps that the servant will harm him with something. So he said: By God, I have not known him.
sentences.i: The stoker feared for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and said to himself: Perhaps the servant will do him some harm. So he said: By God, I do not know him.
sentences.n: The print writes بشي without the hamza (shayʾ, “something”); kept as printed. أن after ربما is the print’s own construction (“perhaps that …”).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّكَ تَكْذِبُ فَإِنَّ مَا هُنَا جَالِسٌ يَقْظَانُ إِلَّا أَنْتَ فَأَنْتَ تَعْرِفُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu wa-allāhi innaka takdhibu fa-inna mā hunā jālisun yaqẓānu illā anta fa-anta taʿrifuhu
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: By God, indeed you lie; for there is not here (any) sitting awake except you; so you know him.
sentences.i: The servant said to him: By God, you are lying! There is no one sitting awake here but you, so you must know him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ وَاللَّهِ أَنَا أَقُولُ لَكَ الْحَقَّ إِنَّ الَّذِي كَانَ يُنْشِدُ الشِّعْرَ رَجُلٌ عَابِرُ طَرِيقٍ وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَزْعَجَنِي وَأَتْلَقَنِي فَاللَّهُ يُجَازِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu wa-allāhi anā aqūlu laka al-ḥaqqa inna alladhī kāna yunshidu al-shiʿra rajulun ʿābiru ṭarīqin wa-huwa alladhī azʿajanī wa-atlaqanī fa-allāhu yujāzīhi
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: By God, I, I tell you the truth: indeed the one who was reciting the poetry (is) a man, a passer-of-a-road; and he (is) the one who disturbed me and … me; so God will requite him.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: By God, I am telling you the truth: the one who was reciting the verses was a man passing by on the road, and it was he who disturbed me and wore me out. May God repay him!
sentences.n: The print has وأتلقني, which does not make a word; it is most likely a misprint for وأتلفني (atlafanī, “ruined me”), and the idiomatic line reads it so.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ إِذَا كُنْتَ تَعْرِفُهُ فَدُلَّنِي عَلَيْهِ وَأَنَا أُمْسِكُهُ وَأَجِي بِهِ عَلَى بَابِ الْمَحَفَّةِ الَّتِي فِيهَا سَيِّدَتُنَا أَوْ أَمْسِكْهُ أَنْتَ بِيَدِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ حَتَّى آتِيَكَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu idhā kunta taʿrifuhu fa-dullanī ʿalayhi wa-anā umsikuhu wa-ajī bihi ʿalā bābi al-maḥaffati allatī fīhā sayyidatunā aw amsikhu anta bi-yadika fa-qāla lahu idhhab anta ḥattā ātiyaka bihi
sentences.l: And the servant said to him: If you know him, guide me to him, and I will seize him and come with him to the door of the litter in which (is) our lady — or seize him, you, with your hand. And he said to him: Go, you, until I bring you him.
sentences.i: The servant said to him: If you know him, show me where he is, and I will take hold of him and bring him to the door of the litter where our lady is — or you can take hold of him yourself. He said to him: Go on, and I will bring him to you.
sentences.n: وَأَجِي is the colloquial short form of أجيء, “I come / I bring”. المحفة is the covered litter in which the lady travels.

sentences.t: فَخَلَاءَ الْخَادِمُ وَانْصَرَفَ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى السِّتِّ وَأَعْلَمَهَا بِذَلِكَ وَقَالَ مَا أَحَدٌ يَعْرِفُهُ وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّاعَابِرُ سَبِيلٍ فَسَكَتَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-khalāʾa al-khādimu wa-ʾnṣarafa wa-dakhala ʿalā al-sitti wa-aʿlamahā bi-dhālika wa-qāla mā aḥadun yaʿrifuhu wa-mā huwa illā ʿābiru sabīlin fa-sakatat
sentences.l: And … the servant, and went away, and entered upon the lady, and informed her of that, and said: There is no one who knows him, and he is not but a passer-of-a-way. And she was silent.
sentences.i: So the servant left him, went away, and came in to the lady and told her what had passed. He said: No one knows him; he is only some passer-by. And she was silent.
sentences.n: The print has فخلاء, which is not a word here; the sense (“and the servant left him”) points to a misprint for فخلاه, and the idiomatic line follows it.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا أَفَاقَ مِنْ غَشْيَتِهِ رَأَى الْقَمَرَ وَصَلَ إِلَى وَسَطِ السَّمَاءِ وَهَبَّ عَلَيْهِ نَسِيمُ الْأَسْحَارِ فَهَيَّجَ فِي قَلْبِهِ الْبَلَابِلَ وَالْأَشْجَانَ فَحَسَّنَ صَوْتَهُ وَأَرَادَأَنْ يُنْشِدَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā ḍawʾu al-makāni fa-innahu lammā afāqa min ghashyatihi raʾā al-qamara waṣala ilā wasaṭi al-samāʾi wa-habba ʿalayhi nasīmu al-asḥāri fa-hayyaja fī qalbihi al-balābila wa-al-ashjāna fa-ḥassana ṣawtahu wa-arāda an yunshida
sentences.l: And as for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, then when he recovered from his swoon he saw the moon had reached the middle of the sky, and the breeze of the dawn-hours blew upon him, and stirred in his heart the cares and the griefs; so he made-fair his voice and wished to recite.
sentences.i: As for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, when he came to himself he saw that the moon had reached the middle of the sky. The breeze of the small hours blew over him and stirred up the pangs and sorrows in his heart, so he cleared and sweetened his voice and wanted to recite.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the previous word (وارادان). الأسحار, plural of سحر, is the last hours before dawn.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ مَاذَا تُرِيدُأَنْ تَصْنَعَ فَقَالَ لَهُ أُرِيدُأَنْ أُنْشِدَ شَيْأً مِنَ الشِّعْرِ لِأُطْفِىَ بِهِ نَارَ قَلْبِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu mādhā turīdu an taṣnaʿa fa-qāla lahu urīdu an unshida shayʾan min al-shiʿri li-uṭfiya bihi nāra qalbī
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: What do you want to do? And he said to him: I want to recite something of poetry, that I may quench with it the fire of my heart.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: What do you mean to do? He said: I want to recite a little poetry, to put out the fire in my heart.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the verbs (تريدان، اريدان) and ends لاطفى with a final ى; read as li-uṭfiya, “that I may quench”.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهُ أَنْتَ مَا عَلِمْتَ بِمَا جَرَى لِي وَمَا سَلِمْتُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ إِلَّا بِأَخْذِي خَاطِرَ الْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: qāla lahu anta mā ʿalimta bi-mā jarā lī wa-mā salimtu min al-qatli illā bi-akhdhī khāṭira al-khādimi
sentences.l: He said to him: You have not known of what happened to me, and I was not safe from the killing except by my taking-hold-of the servant’s mind.
sentences.i: He said to him: You do not know what has happened to me. I only escaped being killed by humouring the servant.
sentences.n: أخذ خاطر فلان, “to take someone’s mind / humour him”, is a colloquial idiom.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَمَاذَا كَانَ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِمَا وَقَعَ فَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي قَدْ أَتَانِى الْخَادِمُ وَأَنْتَ مَغْشِيٌّ عَلَيْكَ وَمَعَهُ عَصًا طَوِيلَةٌ مِنَ اللَّوْزِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-mādhā kāna fa-akhbirnī bi-mā waqaʿa fa-qāla yā sayyidī qad atānī al-khādimu wa-anta maghshiyyun ʿalayka wa-maʿahu ʿaṣan ṭawīlatun mina al-lawzi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: And what was it? So inform me of what befell. And he said: O my lord, the servant came to me while you (were) one swooned-upon, and with him a staff, long, of almond-wood,
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: What was it? Tell me what happened. He said: My lord, the servant came to me while you were lying unconscious, and he had a long almond-wood staff with him,

sentences.t: وَ جَعَلَ يَتَطَلَّعُ فِي وُجُوهِ النَّاسِ وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ وَهُوَ يَسْأَلُ عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ يُنْشِدُ الْأَشْعَارَ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ أَحَدًا مُسْتَيْقِظًا غَيْرِي فَسَأَلَنِي فَقُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَابِرَ سَبِيلٍ فَانْصَرَفَ وَسَلَّمَنِي اللَّهُ مِنْهُ وَإِلَّا كَانَ قَتَلَنِي فَقَالَ لِي إِذَا سَمِعْتَهُ ثَانِيًا فَأْتِ بِهِ عِنْدَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿala yataṭallaʿu fī wujūhi al-nāsi wa-hum nāʾimūna wa-huwa yasʾalu ʿalā man kāna yunshidu al-ashʿāra fa-lam yajid aḥadan mustayqiẓan ghayrī fa-saʾalanī fa-qultu lahu innahu kāna ʿābira sabīlin fa-ʾnṣarafa wa-sallamanī allāhu minhu wa-illā kāna qatalanī fa-qāla lī idhā samiʿtahu thāniyan fa-ʾti bihi ʿindanā
sentences.l: and began to peer into the faces of the people while they (were) sleepers, and he asking about who was reciting the poems; and he found no one awake other than me. So he asked me, and I said to him: Indeed he was a passer-of-a-way. So he went away, and God kept me safe from him, and if not, he would have killed me. And he said to me: If you hear him a second time, bring him to us.
sentences.i: and he started peering into the faces of the people as they slept, asking who had been reciting the poems. He found no one awake but me, so he questioned me, and I told him it was only someone passing by. He went off — God saved me from him; otherwise he would have killed me — but he said to me: If you hear him again, bring him to us.
sentences.n: The print has a stray و at the end of one line and جعل at the start of the next; they are joined here as وجعل.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ذَلِكَ بَكَى وَقَالَ مَنْ يَمْنَعُنِي مِنَ النَّشِيدِ فَأَنَا أُنْشِدُ وَيَجْرِي عَلَيَّ مَا يَجْرِي فَأَنَا قَرُبْتُ مِنْ بِلَادِي وَمَا أُبَالِي مِنْ أَحَدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ḍawʾu al-makāni dhālika bakā wa-qāla man yamnaʿunī mina al-nashīdi fa-anā unshidu wa-yajrī ʿalayya mā yajrī fa-anā qarubtu min bilādī wa-mā ubālī min aḥadin
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard that, he wept and said: Who prevents me from the chant? I shall recite, and what runs will run upon me; for I have drawn near my country, and I do not care about anyone.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard that, he wept and said: Who is going to stop me chanting? I shall recite, and let come what may. I am close to my own country now, and I care about no one.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ أَنْتَ مَا مُرَادُكَ إِلَّاهَلَاكَ نَفْسِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ إِنْشَادِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu anta mā murāduka illā halāka nafsika fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni lā budda min inshādī
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: You, your aim is nothing but the destruction of your soul. And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: There is no escape from my reciting.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: You seem to want nothing but your own destruction. Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: I must recite.
sentences.n: The print runs إلا into the next word (الّاهلاك); the shadda is the edition’s own.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ قَدْ وَقَعَ الْفِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ مِنْ هُنَا وَأَنَا كَانَ نِيَّتِي أَنِّي لَا أُفَارِقُكَ حَتَّى تَدْخُلَ مَدِينَتَكَ وَتَجْتَمِعَ بِأَبِيكَ وَأُمِّكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu qad waqaʿa al-firāqu baynī wa-baynaka min hunā wa-anā kāna niyyatī annī lā ufāriquka ḥattā tadkhula madīnataka wa-tajtamiʿa bi-abīka wa-ummika
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: The parting has fallen between me and you from here; and I — my intention was that I would not leave you until you enter your city and meet with your father and your mother.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: Then there is a parting between you and me from here. I had meant never to leave you until you reached your city and were reunited with your father and mother.
sentences.n: وأنا كان نيتي (“and I, my intention was”) is colloquial: كان with a feminine noun and no agreement. بـ in تجتمع بأبيك means “meet with / join”.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ مَضَى لَكَ عِنْدِي سَنَةٌ وَنِصْفٌ مَا حَصَلَ لَكَ مِنِّي مَا يَضُرُّكَ فَمَا الَّذِي قَامَ بِكَ فِي النَّشِيدِ وَنَحْنُ فِي غَايَةِ التَّعَبِ مِنَ الْمَشْيِ وَالسَّهَرِ وَالنَّاسُ قَدْ هَجَعُوا لِيَسْتَرِيحُوا مِنَ التَّعَبِ وَمُحْتَاجُونَ إِلَى النَّوْمِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad maḍā laka ʿindī sanatun wa-niṣfun mā ḥaṣala laka minnī mā yaḍurruka fa-mā alladhī qāma bika fī al-nashīdi wa-naḥnu fī ghāyati al-taʿabi mina al-mashyi wa-al-saharī wa-al-nāsu qad hajaʿū li-yastarīḥū mina al-taʿabi wa-muḥtājūna ilā al-nawmi
sentences.l: And a year and a half has passed for you with me; nothing has come to you from me that harms you. So what is it that has risen in you for the chanting, while we (are) at the extreme of weariness from the walking and the sleeplessness, and the people have lain down to rest from the weariness, and (are) needing sleep?
sentences.i: You have been with me a year and a half, and nothing has come to you from me that did you any harm. So what has got into you, this chanting, when we are worn out with walking and wakefulness, and the people have lain down to rest from their weariness and need their sleep?
sentences.n: قام بك “rose up in you / came over you” is colloquial for “what possessed you”. The last clause (ومحتاجون) is loosely attached to the people (“and in need of sleep”).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ لَا أَرْجِعُ عَمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni lā arjiʿu ʿammā anā fīhi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: I will not turn back from what I am in.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: I will not give up what I am doing.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَرَّكَتْهُ الْأَشْجَانُ فَبَاحَ بِالْكِتْمَانِ وَجَعَلَ يُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma ḥarrakat-hu al-ashjānu fa-bāḥa bi-al-kitmāni wa-jaʿala yunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then the griefs stirred him, and he revealed the concealment, and began reciting these verses. Poetry:
sentences.i: Then his sorrows stirred him, and he gave away what he had kept hidden, and began to recite these verses. Poetry:
sentences.n: شعر here is the print’s label for the poem that follows.

sentences.t:
قِفْ بِالدِّيَارِ وَحَيِّ الْاَرْبُعَ الدُّرُسَا * وَنَادِهَا فَعَسَاهَا اَنْ تُجِيبْ عَسَى
فَاِنْ اَجَنَّكَ لَيْلٌ مِنْ تَوَحُّشِهَا * اَوْقِدْ مِنَ الشَّوْقِ فِي ظُلُمَاتِهَا قَبَسَا
اِنْ صَلَّ صَلَّ عِذَارَبِهِ فَلَا عَجَبُ * اِنْ يَجْنِي لَسْعًا اَنْ اَجْتَنِي لَعَسَا
يَا جَنَّةً فَارَقْتُهَا النَّفْسُ مُكْرِهَةً * لَوْلَا التَّاسِّي بِدَارِ الْخُلْدِ مُتُّ اَسَى
sentences.tr:
qif bi-al-diyāri wa-ḥayyi al-arbuʿa al-durusā * wa-nādihā fa-ʿasāhā an tujība ʿasā
fa-in ajannaka laylun min tawaḥḥushihā * awqid mina al-shawqi fī ẓulumātihā qabasā
in ṣalla ṣalla ʿidāri-bihi fa-lā ʿajabu * in yajnī lasʿan an ajtanī laʿasā
yā jannatan fāraqtuhā al-nafsu mukrihatan * lawlā al-tāsī bi-dāri al-khuldi muttu asā
sentences.l:
Stand by the abodes and greet the encampments, the effaced ones, * and call to them — perhaps they will answer; perhaps.
And if a night hides you in their desolation, * kindle from longing in their darkness a firebrand.
If a viper hisses, the viper of his cheek-down, no wonder: * (if) he gathers a sting, (that) I gather dark-lip sweetness.
O paradise that the soul left, unwilling — * were it not for the consoling by the Abode of Eternity, I would have died of grief.
sentences.i:
Halt by the dwellings and greet the worn-away campsites, and call to them — perhaps they will answer, perhaps.
And if night closes over you in their desolation, kindle from longing a firebrand in their darkness.
If the viper of his cheek-down hisses, it is no wonder that it stings while I pick the sweetness of his dark lips.
O paradise that my soul left against its will — were it not for the consolation of the Abode of Eternity, I would have died of grief.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. The third line is obscure and the print looks corrupt there (عذاربه, ‘his cheek-down’ run together; يجني لسعا); it is translated tentatively. The Abode of Eternity (دار الخلد) is Paradise.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدَ أَيْضًا هَذَيْنِ الْبَيْتَيْنِ
sentences.tr: wa-anshada ayḍan hādhayni al-baytayni
sentences.l: And he recited also these two verses:
sentences.i: He also recited these two verses:

sentences.t:
كُنَّا وَكَانَتْ لَنَا الْاَيَّامُ خَادِمَةً * وَالشَّمْلُ مُجْتَمِعٌ فِي اَبْهَجِ الْوَطَنِ
مَنْ لِي بِدَارًا حِبَّائِي وَكَانَ بِهَا * ضُوءُ الْمَكَانِ وَفِيهَا نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَنِ
sentences.tr:
kunnā wa-kānat lanā al-ayyāmu khādimatan * wa-al-shamlu mujtamiʿun fī abhaji al-waṭani
man lī bi-dāran ḥibbāʾī wa-kāna bihā * ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-fīhā nuzhatu al-zamāni
sentences.l:
We were, and the days were a servant to us, * and the company gathered in the loveliest homeland.
Who (will give) me a dwelling-place, my beloved ones, in which was * Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and in it Nuzhat al-Zamān?
sentences.i:
We were, and the days served us, with all of us together in the loveliest homeland.
Who will give me back the home of my loved ones, where Ḍawʾ al-Makān once was, and with him Nuzhat al-Zamān?
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as printed. The second line is awkward in the print (بِدَارًا, ضُوءُ with a damma on the ض); read as “who will give me the house of my dear ones”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ صَاحَ ثَلَٰثَ صَيْحَاتٍ ثُمَّ وَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ فَقَامَ الْوَقَّادُ وَغَطَّاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi ṣāḥa thalātha ṣayḥātin thumma waqaʿa ʿalā al-arḍi maghshiyyan ʿalayhi fa-qāma al-waqqādu wa-ghaṭṭāhu
sentences.l: And when he finished his poetry he cried three cries, then fell upon the ground swooned-upon; and the stoker rose and covered him.
sentences.i: When he had finished his poem he cried out three times and fell to the ground in a faint, and the stoker got up and covered him.
sentences.n: ثلث is the print’s defective spelling of ثلاث; it is pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ الْإِنْشَادَ الْأَوَّلَ تَذَكَّرَتْ أَبَاهَا وَأُمَّهَا وَأَخَاهَا وَلَمَّا سَمِعَتِ الْإِنْشَادَ الثَّانِيَ الْمُتَضَمِّنَ لِذِكْرِ اسْمِهَا وَاسْمِ أَخِيهَا وَمَعَا هِدِهِمَا بَكَتْ وَصَاحَتْ عَلَى الْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat nuzhatu al-zamāni al-inshāda al-awwala tadhakkarat abāhā wa-ummahā wa-akhāhā wa-lammā samiʿati al-inshāda al-thāniya al-mutaḍammina li-dhikri ismihā wa-ismi akhīhā wa-maʿāhidihimā bakat wa-ṣāḥat ʿalā al-khādimi
sentences.l: And when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard the first reciting, she remembered her father and her mother and her brother; and when she heard the second reciting, the one containing mention of her name and the name of her brother and their haunts, she wept and cried out at the servant,
sentences.i: When Nuzhat al-Zamān heard the first recitation, she remembered her father, her mother and her brother; and when she heard the second recitation, which contained her own name, her brother’s name and the places they had known, she wept and cried out to the servant,
sentences.n: The print splits ومعاهدهما into two (ومعا هدهما); read as one word, maʿāhid, “haunts, places frequented”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ إِنَّ الَّذِي أَنْشَدَ أَوَّلًا أَنْشَدَ ثَانِيًا وَسَمِعْتُهُ قَرِيبًا مِنِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْتِنِي بِهِ لَأُنَبِّهَنَّ عَلَيْكَ الْحَاجِبَ فَيَضْرِبَكَ وَيَطْرُدَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu waylaka inna alladhī anshada awwalan anshada thāniyan wa-samiʿtuhu qarīban minnī wa-allāhi in lam taʾtinī bihi la-unabbihanna ʿalayka al-ḥājiba fa-yaḍribaka wa-yaṭrudaka
sentences.l: and said to him: Woe to you! The one who recited first has recited second, and I heard him near me. By God, if you do not bring him to me, I will certainly alert the chamberlain against you, and he will beat you and drive you out.
sentences.i: and said to him: Shame on you! The man who recited first has recited again, and I heard him close to me. By God, if you do not bring him to me, I will have the chamberlain told about you, and he will beat you and throw you out.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ خُذْ هَذِهِ الْمِائَةَ دِينَارٍ وَأَعْطِهِ أَبَاهَا وَائْتِنِي بِهِ بِرِفْقٍ وَلَا تَضُرَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin khudh hādhihi al-miʾata dīnārin wa-aʿṭihi abāhā wa-ʾtinī bihi bi-rifqin wa-lā taḍurrahu
sentences.l: But take these hundred dinars, and give him … , and bring me with him with gentleness, and do not harm him.
sentences.i: But take these hundred dinars, give them to him, and bring him to me gently, and do him no harm.
sentences.n: The print has اباها (“his father”) after أعطه, which does not fit; the sense calls for إياها (“give it to him”), and the idiomatic line follows that.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ أَبَى ادْفَعْ لَهُ هَذَا الْكِيسَ الَّذِي فِيهِ أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ فَإِنْ أَبَى فَاتْرُكْهُ وَاعْرِفْ مَكَانَهُ وَصَنْعَتَهُ وَمِنْ أَيِّ الْبِلَادِ هُوَ وَارْجِعْ إِلَيَّ بِسُرْعَةٍ وَلَا تَغِبْ
sentences.tr: fa-in abā idfaʿ lahu hādhā al-kīsa alladhī fīhi alfu dīnārin fa-in abā fa-ʾtrukhu wa-ʾʿrif makānahu wa-ṣanʿatahu wa-min ayyi al-bilādi huwa wa-ʾrjiʿ ilayya bi-surʿatin wa-lā taghib
sentences.l: And if he refuses, pay him this purse in which (is) a thousand dinars; and if he refuses, leave him, and learn his place and his craft and from which of the lands he (is), and return to me with speed, and do not be absent.
sentences.i: If he refuses, give him this purse with a thousand dinars in it. If he still refuses, leave him, but find out where he lives, what his trade is and what country he comes from, and come back to me quickly. Do not linger.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُ—بَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night. The print’s last word is damaged (الم—باح, with a dash inside it); it is read as the formula’s usual al-mubāḥ.
